audits.title: Audit on Prescribing Practice of Depot Antipsychotic Injections in the Adult Community Mental Health Service
audits.standard: BNF, Trust and Maudsley guidelines for long-acting antipsychotic prescribing
audits.setting: Depot clinic, City East Adult Community Mental Health Team, Leicester

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for licensed indication and dose/frequency within BNF range; 14% received polypharmacy; 86% had regular outpatient review; only 46% had side effect review.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations included better documentation, automatic review reminders, a clinic checklist and re-audit.
audits.citation: Ray M, Rao S. Audit on Prescribing Practice of Depot Antipsychotic Injections in the Adult Community Mental Health Service. European Psychiatry. 2017;41(S1):S277-S277. doi:10.1016/j.eurpsy.2017.02.116.

audits.title: Re-Audit of Compliance With Standard Operating Procedure for Prescription of Depot Medication Within the Wolverhampton Older Adult Services
audits.standard: BCHFT standard operating procedure: 15 standards for depot prescription writing
audits.setting: Wolverhampton Older Adult Enhanced Community Mental Health Teams, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Standard 3 (signed, dated, name printed) 75%; Standard 7 (interval using the word 'every') 19%.

audits.intervention: Memory aid for prescribers placed at the front of depot card folders.

cycle2.result: 6 of 15 standards 100%; Standard 3 fell to 15%; Standard 7 improved to 31%.

audits.other_findings: Standard 3 non-compliance was mainly due to no space for printing prescriber's name; depot cards to be revised to include signature and name columns.
audits.citation: Ling C, Prasanna A. Re-Audit of Compliance With Standard Operating Procedure for Prescription of Depot Medication Within the Wolverhampton Older Adult Services. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S164-S164. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.462.

audits.title: Re-Audit of Prescribing Responsibility for Antipsychotic Depots for Shared Care Patients(PRAD-SCP)
audits.standard: GMMMG Shared Care Pathway: prescribing of depots for stable patients transferred to GP; target 100%
audits.setting: Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton community mental health team depot clinics

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 96%; first generation antipsychotics 98%; paliperidone and risperidone 94%; aripiprazole 91%.

audits.other_findings: One team was 99% compliant overall. The 100% target was still not met; transfers between teams were a weak point.
audits.citation: Ziriki A, Webb C, Olowoyo O, Lee K. Re-Audit of Prescribing Responsibility for Antipsychotic Depots for Shared Care Patients(PRAD-SCP). BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S189-S189. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.489.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Psychiatrist Reviews of Patients on Depot Antipsychotic Medication Under a General Adult Community Mental Health Service in North Norfolk
audits.standard: Maudsley prescribing guidelines: all patients on long-term antipsychotics seen by responsible psychiatrist at least once a year; target 100%
audits.setting: General adult community mental health service, North Norfolk

cycle1.result: 28/47 (approximately 60%) reviewed by a psychiatrist in the last year; 19 (approximately 40%) not reviewed.

audits.other_findings: Of the 19 not reviewed, only 8 had been offered an appointment. Findings discussed with the community team manager to arrange prompt reviews.
audits.citation: Olajide O. Clinical Audit of Psychiatrist Reviews of Patients on Depot Antipsychotic Medication Under a General Adult Community Mental Health Service in North Norfolk. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S253-S254. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.613.

audits.title: Shots in Practice: An Audit of Depot Antipsychotics in Pakistan’s Outpatient Psychiatry Department
audits.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition) for long-acting injectable antipsychotics
audits.setting: Outpatient department, Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore

cycle1.result: All patients on fluphenazine decanoate with a concurrent second antipsychotic (100% polypharmacy); 78% informed of side effects; none had post-injection observation; no test doses given; no baseline ECG or physical health assessment; fluphenazine used in rapid tranquillisation.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations included staff training on Maudsley guidance, test dose protocols, mandatory baseline ECG, revised rapid tranquillisation protocol and regular re-audit.
audits.citation: Suleman A, Abdullah F, Anjum A, Shafi A. Shots in Practice: An Audit of Depot Antipsychotics in Pakistan’s Outpatient Psychiatry Department. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S281-S282. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10683.

audits.title: Optimising Procyclidine Prescribing and Monitoring in Patients on Long-Acting Injectable Antipsychotics: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: Trust guidelines: starting dose 2.5mg, review every 3–4 months, attempted withdrawal after 3 months
audits.setting: Dartford, Gravesham and Swanley CMHT, Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 14/36 (39%) on regular procyclidine; 93% had recorded reviews; 0% on recommended starting regimen; no withdrawal plans documented.

audits.intervention: Team-wide dissemination of findings and standardised prompts for dose-reduction discussions at reviews.

cycle2.result: 18/100 (18%) on procyclidine; dose reduced in 3/18 (17%) and reduction discussed in 4/18 (22%); 44% received active de-prescribing intervention or discussion.

audits.other_findings: Project followed a fatal procyclidine overdose; 1/18 (6%) needed a dose increase.
audits.citation: Gautam P, Mitchell S, Osoba L. Optimising Procyclidine Prescribing and Monitoring in Patients on Long-Acting Injectable Antipsychotics: A Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S153-S154. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11383.
